chapter: Funeral customs, Pickwick band and later years
title: Which churches hired bands: Catholic, Protestant and Jewish funerals
summary: Love explains that Catholic funerals bring the body to church without music and that Protestant groups hire bands, and recalls a Jewish wedding in Shreveport.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: That's something that reminded me of something else I wanted to ask you. What different religions did you used to play for? Religion?
Yeah. Like Baptists and… Catholic. You all did play music for Catholic funerals? In flag one, that's all they were.
Catholic. No, I mean music for funerals.
What religions would hire a band?
Oh, Baptist people, art fella. Catholics, they don't have music.

They never did? Well, once in a while like that, some fella belonged to the Catholic Church. If he desires music and asked for it, say he want music when he dies, when he dies, the Catholic Church, if you desire music and ask for it, you know, say you want music when you die, the band will come bring your body to church but they don't play. They just march behind, you know, the grand marshal and they bring the body into church and the band waits for you. And when they come out of church they don't play. When they get in the next block of Wesleyan Church then they start playing. Then I'd like the Methodists they'll have, and the Baptists, and the Elves and different societies like that, but the Catholics don't
have anything. Well I knew they didn't anymore, I just wondered

if they used to. No they never did. If a fellow desires isn't going with the Catholic, then they can bring them to the Catholic Church, but they don't have that music. They walk, when they get in that block they don't play, they walk to the church and they bring the band, this band, and wait for them until the family goes. They get back in line and they get in the next block they play. But they won't do like that church. There's nothing in the Catholic religion, in the Bible, you see. Most Catholics are the Father of Christ, Jesus Christ, and he didn't have no music. And he could do that and you. Now, the Jewish people, it's funny, I remember in Shreepo we played for a Jew win. We had our uniform and everything on, you know, went into it. We was up in the balcony, went up there and I went up there and pulled my hat off, you know. Went in up there and the fellow come there, took my hat and said, put your hat on in there. I said no, I'm going to put my hat on there and pull it off. You know, you go out in there and pull it off. When you go out of the door, when you go outside, you take it off. That's funny, isn't it? Differently, you know, I felt. I said nothing down, you know, and took my hat off, you know, had it on my lap. The fellow come from way downstairs up there, seen that, you know. And then he went up there and said, put my hat on. And he said, put my hat on. I said, no. Can't do that. You're going to do it if you stay in there. You slapped it on. Pull it off when you go outside. So when you go outside take that off. Don't wear it off. And another thing I see them do after they marry, they got something in two glasses that they gave them, the fellow gave them his wife. She drank and he took one and he drank like that. And they break that glass. Throw it down. Bam! Break that glass all over. I never did find out what that was. It's wine. Huh? It's wine. But they break the glass. That's a meaning to that.
